hypotheses.justification: After `gradedBracket_gradedMkZero, gradedRestrict_gradedMk, coe_mk` the goal is `h ⁅g,g'⁆ = μ (a g) (b g') - μ (a g') (b g)`; htrivM only enters through `apply_commutatorElement_of_smul_eq_self`, where it is used solely to make `a` additive. It is not needed. With htrivA and htrivP, `hh.apply_mul_of_smul_eq_self htrivA htrivP` gives h(uv) = h u + h v + F(u,v) with F(x,y) = μ(a x)(b y). F is additive in y because b is a homomorphism (`map_mul_of_smul_eq_self_of_mem_Z1 htrivA b.2`). Comparing h((xy)z) with h(x(yz)) gives F(y,z) - F(xy,z) + F(x,yz) - F(x,y) = 0, hence F(xy,z) = F(x,z) + F(y,z). So F is biadditive whatever the action on M, and a is never required to be additive. Expanding h(x y x⁻¹ y⁻¹) with h 1 = 0 and h x⁻¹ = -h x + F(x,x) gives F(x,y) - F(y,x), the stated right-hand side. htrivM does not appear in the statement, so dropping it is harmless for elaboration. Not checked whether htrivM and htrivA can be removed together; each can be removed on its own.

Symmetric argument, keeping htrivM and htrivP. Here a is additive (`map_mul_of_smul_eq_self_of_mem_Z1 htrivM a.2`) and h(uv) = h u + h v + F(u,v) with F(x,y) = μ(a x)(x • b y), which is just hh.apply_mul with trivial action on P. Associativity of h gives F(y,z) - F(xy,z) + F(x,yz) - F(x,y) = 0. Expanding this with the cocycle law b(yz) = b y + y • b z and additivity of a leaves μ(a y)(y • b z) = μ(a y)(x • y • b z) for all x, y, z. Taking x = y⁻¹ gives F(x,y) = μ(a x)(b y). This is additive in x since a is, and additive in y since μ(a x)(b(yz)) = μ(a x)(b y + y • b z) = μ(a x)(b y) + μ(a x)(b z). The same commutator expansion then yields μ(a x)(b y) - μ(a y)(b x). htrivA does not appear in the statement. Each of htrivM and htrivA can be removed separately; not checked whether both can be removed together.
